Monthly and annual flow on FWA segments

Source: R/wet_segment_monthly.R
wet_segment_monthly.Rd

Reads mean flow per month on Freshwater Atlas stream segments, by source, in the shape of wet_station_monthly() (month 1-12, and 0 for the mean annual flow), so a gauge comparison is a join on month after wet_station_snap().

Usage

wet_segment_monthly(
  conn,
  segments,
  source = c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance"),
  from = c("published", "fwapg"),
  scenario = "historical",
  groups = NULL,
  catalog = NULL
)

Arguments

conn

NULL, or a DBI::DBIConnection to Postgres: the database wet_db_load() wrote to for from = "published", fwapg for from = "fwapg".

segments

linear_feature_ids. Repeats are read once.

source

Any of "pcic_routed" (PCIC's routed flow placed on the FWA) and "wet_balance" (wet's open water balance). Left out, every source from holds: both for "published", "pcic_routed" for "fwapg".

from

"published" or "fwapg", as described above.

scenario

Scenario of the published product, e.g. "historical". fwapg's run is "historical" only.

groups

Optional watershed group codes that hold the segments. A segment outside them reads as missing.

catalog

For parts read without conn: the output of wet_catalog(), which is read when NULL.

Value

data.frame(linear_feature_id, month, q_m3s, source), ordered by source as given, segment as given and month. A segment with no value for a source has all 13 rows, with q_m3s NA, so missing coverage stays visible after a join.

Where the values come from

With from = "published" (the default) the values are wet's published product, discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly (wet_catalog()): from the Postgres table discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly that wet_db_load() writes when conn is given, otherwise straight from the parquet parts the manifest lists, through duckdb. Its routed month 0 is the plain mean of the twelve months, and fresh joins the same rows.

With from = "fwapg", pcic_routed is read from fwapg's own routed table (pcic.discharge_monthly), the run PCIC's hydromosaic made with PNWNAmet forcing, historical, averaged over 1981-2010 (model, scenario and period PNWNAmet, historical, 1981-2010), with month 0 computed by the same rule as the published one: the mean of the twelve months, NA unless all twelve have flow. That table is loaded by the NewGraphEnvironment fork of fwapg (load/pcic_schema.sql, load/pcic.sql, then load/pcic_run.sql per run), not by upstream fwapg; a table without the run's rows is an error. Scoring the table before it is published (scripts/pcic_routed_compare.R) reads it this way.

Reading parts with no groups reads the segment ID column of every part (about half a minute for a few segments over HTTPS, and nearly the whole 1.8 GB for many). The parts are sorted by watershed group, so naming the groups that hold the segments keeps a read to seconds. Parts are read in place, unlike wet_db_load(), which checks each one's size and md5 first: a read during a publish can mix two builds, so retry once it completes.

See also

wet_flow_window() for flow over a date window; wet_station_monthly() for the gauge's side of a comparison.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Buck Creek at its mouth, where gauge 08EE013 sits, from the published
# parts over HTTPS (about 3 s)
q <- wet_segment_monthly(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")
reshape(q[q$month > 0, ], idvar = c("linear_feature_id", "month"),
        timevar = "source", direction = "wide")

# the same from Postgres, after wet_db_load()
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "fwapg")
wet_segment_monthly(conn, 17094080)
} # }
